newsitem.title: GERMANY: SWIMMING-EUROPEAN RECORD DOUBLES FOR SJOBERG AND VOELKER.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-EUROPEAN RECORD DOUBLES FOR SJOBERG AND VOELKER.

text.p: Johanna Sjoberg and her victim, Sandra Voelker, produced European records for the second time in 24 hours at the European sprints and short-course swimming championships on Saturday.
In an exact repeat of Friday's events, Olympic medallist Voelker had to digest defeat by the Swede before producing a record of her own in the 25-metre Neptun pool.
On Friday, Sjoberg beat the German and broke the European short-course 50 butterfly mark before Voelker obliterated Franziska van Almsick's 100 freestyle record.

On Saturday, the Swede again trumped Voelker in the butterfly, winning the 100 event and earning a congratulatory hug from her German rival before Voelker swept away with the title and European record in the 50 freestyle.
"I was a bit disappointed after losing the 100 butterfly," Voelker said. "My performance in the freestyle sprint was all the more convincing after a break of only 25 minutes.
"The prize money for records (5,000 marks/$3,420 each) are a special incentive. The shops should be pleased -- I haven't bought any Christmas presents yet."
Sjoberg narrowly led Voelker at the halfway mark of the 100 butterfly but pulled away on the last two lengths to win in 58.80 seconds to Voelker's 59.44.

Sjoberg's time eclipsed the 59.35 European mark set by East German Kornelia Gressler in this pool on December 21 1985 and was not far outside the 58.29 world mark posted by American Misty Hyman in Quebec City earlier this month.
"I was quite nervous before the start because I reckoned I had a chance against Sandra Voelker after winning yesterday. I was really going for the record too," Sjoberg said.

Voelker bounced back to win the 50 freestyle in 24.67, slicing 0.08 seconds from the European short-course record she shared with fellow German van Almsick, one of several prominent absentees from these four-day championships.

Germany topped the medals table with 10 titles after five wins on the third day from Voelker, Jens Kruppa (men's 100 breaststroke), Lars Conrad (men's 200 freestyle), Antje Buschschulte (women's 100 backstroke) and the men's 4x50 freestyle relay.
Britain clinched two golds, thanks to Mark Foster in the men's 50 butterfly and Susan Rolph in the women's 100 individual medley.

Foster, who came close to elimination in the heats as slowest qualifier, produced a determined swim in the final to win in 23.91 -- outside his world best 23.45 but too good for nearest rivals Fabian Hieronimus of Germany (24.07) and Jonas Akesson of Sweden (24.25).

Rolph had a hectic day. Eight minutes after taking the silver behind Voelker in the 50 freestyle she returned to win the medley in 1:01.94, just 0.04 seconds ahead of fast-finishing Slovak Martina Moravcova.
But Ian Wilson, 1995 world short-course silver medallists, was unable to make it a British golden treble, finishing second to 18-year-old Ukrainian Igor Snitko in the 1,500 freestyle.

Poland's Alicja Peczak, who served a two-year ban for steroid use, won the women's 200 metres breaststroke to cap the bronzes she gained at the European long-course and world short- course championships in 1995.
Peczak, third in Friday's 100 breaststroke, overhauled Sweden's Lena Eriksson 50 metres from home and stretched away to win in 2:26.11 from Slovenia's Alenka Kejzar.
